title: VLAN Segmentation Lab
objective: Configure VLAN 10 (Faculty) and VLAN 20 (Students) on a Cisco Catalyst 2960 switch, assign access ports, and demonstrate network isolation between different broadcast domains.

configurations.SW1:
enable
configure terminal
hostname SW1

vlan 10
 name Faculty
exit

vlan 20
 name Students
exit

interface FastEthernet0/1
 description Connected to PC1 (Faculty)
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 no shutdown
exit

interface FastEthernet0/2
 description Connected to PC2 (Students)
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 20
 no shutdown
exit

interface FastEthernet0/3
 description Connected to PC3 (Faculty)
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 no shutdown
exit

interface FastEthernet0/4
 description Connected to PC4 (Students)
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 20
 no shutdown
exit

end
write memory

instructions: Open Cisco Packet Tracer and create a new workspace.
Place one Cisco Catalyst 2960 switch (SW1) and four generic PCs (PC1, PC2, PC3, PC4).
Connect the PCs to SW1 using Copper Straight-Through cables:
Configure static IP addresses on all PCs (Desktop -> IP Configuration):
Click SW1 -> CLI, press Enter, and paste the SW1 configuration commands.
Verify that the switch ports are configured in their respective VLANs.
verification: On SW1 CLI, run 'show vlan brief' to verify VLAN 10 contains Fa0/1, Fa0/3 and VLAN 20 contains Fa0/2, Fa0/4.
Test Intra-VLAN connectivity (VLAN 10): From PC1, ping PC3 at 192.168.10.20. Expected: Success (4 replies).
Test Intra-VLAN connectivity (VLAN 20): From PC2, ping PC4 at 192.168.20.20. Expected: Success (4 replies).
Test Inter-VLAN isolation (VLAN 10 to VLAN 20): From PC1, ping PC2 at 192.168.20.10. Expected: Request timed out (100% loss) because VLANs are isolated Layer 2 broadcast domains without a router.
